risks.title: HCP pricing increases since Runs 1+2
risks.description: HCP Vault Dedicated (standard_small) pricing may have changed since the $321.81 historical accrual (Runs 1+2, October). If the hourly rate has increased, an equivalent ceremony duration will cost more.
risks.mitigation: Human operator confirms current pricing from HCP portal BEFORE any cost authorization decision. Never use $321.81 as a ceiling — it is historical reference only.
risks.residual_risk: LOW — if pricing confirmation procedure is followed

risks.title: Ceremony runtime exceeds authorized maximum
risks.description: Unexpected delays (provisioning, CloudWatch configuration, verification retries) can cause the ceremony to run longer than the authorized maximum, resulting in unauthorized cost accrual.
risks.mitigation: 1. Hard maximum runtime set and recorded before provisioning. 2. Operator watchdog (FP-007 remediation) emits warning at 75% and mandatory stop signal at 100% of max runtime. 3. No exploratory debugging against paid infrastructure.
risks.residual_risk: MEDIUM — cloud billing is delayed; watchdog estimates cost but cannot guarantee dollar cap

risks.title: Billing delay causes overspend before operator can respond
risks.description: HCP cloud billing is not real-time. An operator tracking estimated cost via runtime cannot rely on provider-reported accruals as a hard cap. By the time a billing alert fires, the actual cost may already exceed the authorized maximum.
risks.mitigation: 1. Operator watchdog is time-based (wall clock), not cost-based. 2. Authorized maximum runtime is the binding control, not a dollar amount. 3. Cost ceiling is derived from hourly rate * max_runtime. 4. Document explicitly that runtime watchdog does NOT provide a guaranteed dollar cap.
risks.residual_risk: LOW — time-based watchdog is more reliable than cost-based

risks.title: Partial teardown leaves billable HCP resources running
risks.description: A teardown failure (network interruption, Terraform state corruption, operator error) may leave the HCP Vault cluster running after the ceremony ends, causing ongoing cost accrual until manually destroyed.
risks.mitigation: 1. Staged teardown path verified offline before ceremony. 2. Provider-side deletion (HCP console) is a backup to Terraform destroy. 3. Billing evidence captured AFTER teardown completes to confirm zero ongoing accrual. 4. Hard teardown deadline regardless of ceremony state.

risks.title: Prior $321.81 authorization treated as valid for Run 3
risks.description: An operator or reviewer may incorrectly believe the $321.81 historical figure from ceremony_state.yaml constitutes an available spending envelope for Run 3. It does not — it is consumed.
risks.mitigation: 1. run3_cost_authorization_request.json explicitly marks all financial values null. 2. Pricing evidence schema requires fresh confirmation. 3. Tests assert that $321.81 is never used as a cost ceiling in any authorization logic.

risks.title: Unattended ceremony run overnight
risks.description: If the operator leaves the ceremony running unattended (e.g., overnight), and the watchdog is not active, the cluster could accrue cost far beyond the authorized maximum.
risks.mitigation: 1. ceremony_state.yaml explicitly prohibits unattended overnight execution. 2. Hard teardown deadline set before ceremony begins. 3. Operator watchdog emits hard stop signal at maximum runtime.

risks.title: AWS costs underestimated
risks.description: AWS CloudWatch costs for ceremony-scale Vault audit traffic are negligible (KB-scale volume at $0.50/GB ingestion). However, if audit volume is much higher than expected, costs could be marginally higher.
risks.mitigation: CloudWatch log retention and cost confirmed negligible in cost_containment.md. AWS IAM resources have no direct cost.

aggregate_risk_posture: MEDIUM — primary driver is FR-001 (unverified pricing) and FR-002 (runtime overrun). Both are mitigated if the operator follows the pricing confirmation procedure and operator watchdog is active.
risk_acceptance_conditions: Human operator has confirmed current HCP pricing from the HCP portal
requested_max_cost_usd is set to a value the approver explicitly accepts
Operator watchdog is running during the ceremony
Teardown procedure is verified offline before ceremony begins
Historical $321.81 figure is not used as a ceiling
